claim: Instances within one structured object need not be treated as i.i.d.
basis: Zhou et al. 2009 directly motivates relational MIL.
boundary: Do not generalize to every task without testing.

claim: Relations among instances can carry useful structural information.
basis: Supported conceptually by relational MIL, SketchGraphs, scene-graph and grammar traditions.
boundary: This does not prove garment relations are recoverable.

claim: Primitive geometry alone is insufficient for semantics.
basis: Contextual sketch-recognition literature supports this distinction.
boundary: Do not claim a specific garment semantic ontology is established.

claim: Graphs can encode typed geometric or semantic relations rather than only similarity.
basis: Supported by CAD constraints, scene graphs, grammar literature.
boundary: Do not reduce relation inference to Euclidean proximity.

claim: Incorrect graph structure can harm learning.
basis: Explicitly cautioned in Zhou et al. 2009 image categorization discussion.
boundary: This is a design warning, not a quantified WeaveAI result.

claim: Programs can represent hierarchy, attachment, repetition, symmetry and parameterized structure.
basis: Supported by graphics-program, Vitruvion and ShapeAssembly traditions.
boundary: Do not claim garment-program recovery has been demonstrated.

claim: Probabilistic program induction is a precedent for structured few-shot concept learning.
boundary: Do not claim identical few-shot behavior will transfer to garments.

claim: MCA + probability + geometry may provide a useful node representation for garment sketches.
basis: This is our synthesis across sparse morphology and structured sketch literature.
boundary: Requires experiment; not established by cited papers.

claim: Typed garment relations may be modeled as latent probabilistic edge variables.
basis: Motivated by NRI and probabilistic graphical modeling.
boundary: Static garment sketches differ from interacting dynamical systems.

claim: Graph-structured MIL may be useful under garment-level supervision.
basis: Motivated by relational MIL and weak-supervision needs.
boundary: Requires a validated graph and suitable bag semantics.

claim: WeaveAI has already established a novel garment grammar.
basis: No empirical evidence or novelty audit supports this.

claim: MCA components correspond directly to silhouette, seam, fold, text, or ornament.
basis: Morphological separation is not semantic labeling.
boundary: Do not claim without direct evidence.

claim: A GNN is required for WeaveAI.
basis: No demonstrated failure of simpler graph methods yet.
boundary: Graph kernel / explicit rules / probabilistic models remain viable baselines.

claim: The final WeaveAI architecture is MCA + Bayesian inference + GNN + MIL + grammar + program synthesis.
basis: Current work is a conceptual synthesis, not an architecture freeze.
boundary: Do not present as final architecture.

claim: Edge existence can be determined solely by distance in embedding space.
basis: Our synthesis explicitly distinguishes similarity from structural relation.
boundary: Do not use as default assumption.
